blocks.text: Laura lowered herself against the ventilator and put her hands in her lap.
The metal was cold through her coat. The brass funnel filled the space ahead.
Daniel took the rope from the top of the vent.
“In front,” she said, holding out her wrists.
“Yes. Let him see them.”

He passed the rope around the housing and brought it across her middle. Laura lifted her elbows while he worked, then lowered them when he asked. The turns held her upper arms against her sides, with her forearms resting across her lap.
She watched him wind the remaining length around her wrists. A short span joined the binding at her hands to the rope across her coat. He drew it firm and finished the knot beside her hip.
Laura pulled her hands apart.
The rope held.
“That'll do.”
Daniel sat back. Laura looked past him into the brass mouth, her boots planted on the gravel.
blocks.alt: Daniel finishes the ordinary rope holding fully costumed Laura against the low rooftop vent while bodyless Luke watches from beside the idle collector.

blocks.text: Luke drifted nearer. His eyes followed the rope around the metal housing.
“Can she get loose?”
Laura looked up at him.
“I'm sitting right here.”
“She only has to stay there until he comes,” Daniel said.
He fetched folded gray canvas from the stairhouse.
Laura shifted against the bindings, already uncomfortable.
Daniel spread the canvas over the glass and coils, disguising them as unfinished equipment.
He left the brass mouth uncovered. On the western side, a lifted fold gave him access to the meters and switches.
Daniel crouched behind the trolley until only his shoes showed.
“A little farther back.”
He drew them in.
Luke settled beside the western controls, between the collector and warehouse wall.
She turned her wrists together. The rope dragged across the seam of one glove.
“Ready,” Daniel said from behind the canvas.
Laura looked above the parapet.
If nothing happened, they would both see it. Daniel and Luke were waiting for something she had never tried on purpose.
She opened her mouth.
“I need help.”
The words went out over the roof. A truck changed gear in the street below.
She waited. The sky stayed empty.
Flaming Head had felt her need beside the lake. Saying the words had not been enough.
Now she was thinking about Daniel's shoes and the rope on her wrists.
She let her head rest against the vent.
A door slammed below the roof. For an instant she was back in the apartment, holding the door after her boyfriend had left.
She held on to how it had felt to want an answer. Under everything she intended to do here, that part was easy to find.
“I just need somebody to help me,” Laura said. “Please.”
blocks.alt: Laura sits with her gloved wrists bound in her lap, her face and mouth clear, looking toward the twilight sky as she deliberately asks Flaming Head for help.

blocks.text: She loosened her clenched hands and watched the sky.
Flaming Head turned above the shoreline rocks.
He had been watching a boat turn toward the harbor when the feeling reached him.
Someone needed help.
The feeling drew him inland.
Something in that need was familiar.
He remembered Laura practicing in the costume he had made. At their last meeting, she had told him she was working with Daniel Orkleson.
He had warned her. She had refused to say what they were doing.
Flaming Head left the water behind and flew toward the lower industrial roofs.
blocks.alt: A bright, healthy Flaming Head turns away from Lake Erie and flies inland toward the familiar sense that someone needs him.

blocks.text: He followed the familiar need inland toward a taller stretch of brickwork.
A lower roof lay in shadow beneath its last sunlit windows.
A movement caught his eye near its northern edge.
He went higher.
Laura heard gravel shift beside the collector.
Luke rose to look beyond the vent.
“There.”
Daniel's hand appeared beneath the lifted fold of canvas. He pointed once toward the roof, and Luke dropped out of sight beside the control box.
A small orange light moved above the neighboring roof.
Her wrists pressed together as the light approached.
The light stopped.
For a moment she thought he had seen enough and would go away.
“Please,” she said again, more quietly.
She saw him turn.
From above the parapet, Flaming Head could see the top of the ventilator and Laura's hair against it.
He moved around the housing until her face came into view.
She was sitting on the roof. Rope passed around her coat and disappeared behind the metal box. Her gloved hands lay together in her lap, bound too.
He stopped above her.
Behind him, a gray sheet covered a trolley. Its exposed brass funnel pointed toward her.
He moved slightly to one side. The funnel caught his light.
Laura tried to lift her hands. The rope drew tight across her coat and stopped them.
He looked back at her face.
Whatever had happened between them beside the lake, she was tied here now. Leaving her would mean leaving her with whoever had done it.
Flaming Head came lower, until Laura could see the concern in his eyes instead of only the brightness of the flame.
blocks.alt: Flaming Head arrives beside bound Laura on the established rooftop; the collector waits beneath gray canvas with its brass intake open, still switched off.

blocks.text: “Laura?”
The word reached her alone, inside her mind. His mouth had not moved. Behind the collector, Daniel and Luke heard nothing.
For a moment, her answer caught in her throat.
Behind him, the canvas hung still over the collector. There was no hum.
Laura looked into the little face that had come when she asked.
“Help me,” she said.
